stories.title: Engine abstraction layer (testable synth)
stories.user_story: As a developer, I want the Controller to depend on a synth interface (not the cgo FluidSynth type) so that domain logic can be tested without audio hardware.
stories.description: Introduce a Synth interface in internal/engine (NoteOn/NoteOff/CC/PitchBend/SelectProgram/SetChannelVolume/SetChannelPan/AllNotesOff/Panic/SetMasterGain/LoadSoundFont). The real *engine.Engine satisfies it. Provide a FakeEngine test double that records every call. Refactor app.NewController to accept the interface.
steps_to_reproduce: Build the project: go build ./...
Run go vet ./internal/app to confirm Controller compiles against the interface
In a test, construct a Controller with FakeEngine and call NoteOn; inspect FakeEngine.Calls
acceptance_criteria: Controller no longer references C/cgo types directly
*engine.Engine implements engine.Synth (compile-time assertion)
FakeEngine records ordered calls with channel/key/vel/cc args
go test ./internal/app runs with NO audio device and NO cgo engine instance
stories.fix_solution: Introduced engine.Synth (internal/engine/synth.go): a cgo-free control interface (LoadSoundFont/SelectProgram/NoteOn/NoteOff/CC/PitchBend/AllNotesOff/SetChannelVolume/SetChannelPan/SetMasterGain/Panic) with a compile-time assertion that *engine.Engine implements it. Refactored Controller.eng to engine.Synth and NewController to accept it (guarding a nil MIDI manager for tests). Added FakeEngine (records ordered calls) so the whole domain layer tests with no audio/cgo. Tests green: ordered-call recording + single-layer note routing.

stories.title: Song & part persistence (SQLite)
stories.user_story: As a gigging keyboardist, I want songs and their ordered parts (with full per-keyboard state incl. effects) stored in SQLite so my set list is durable.
stories.description: Extend internal/db with CRUD: CreateSong/ListSongs/RenameSong/DeleteSong, AddPart/ListParts/ReorderParts/SavePartChannels/DeletePart. Extend the part_channels schema with chorus_* and delay_* columns (migration). Provide a thin app service that maps db.Part <-> app.Scene/Part.
steps_to_reproduce: Open a DB at a temp path (or :memory:)
Create a song, add parts, set channel sound+fx, close
Reopen and read back; values match
Delete the song; parts are gone (cascade)
acceptance_criteria: Schema migrates to add chorus/delay columns idempotently
Parts keep a stable sort_order; reorder persists
part_channels round-trips sound, mix, split, transpose, pan, chorus(2), delay(3)
Foreign-key cascade removes parts when a song is deleted
stories.fix_solution: Extended internal/db: added per-keyboard FX columns (chorus_on/rate/depth, delay_on/time/feedback/mix) to part_channels via an idempotent addColumnIfMissing migration (PRAGMA table_info check + ALTER TABLE), enabled FK cascade through the DSN (_pragma=foreign_keys(1)), and added the FX fields to db.Channel. New internal/db/crud.go implements CreateSong/ListSongs/RenameSong/DeleteSong, AddPart (auto sort_order + default channels), SetPartChannel (UPSERT), ListParts/GetPart (channels loaded), SavePartMeta, DeletePart, ReorderParts (tx), CountParts. Verified by a godog feature (3 scenarios/18 steps: ordered parts, full FX round-trip, cascade delete) and a migration unit test that opens a pre-FX DB and confirms columns are added with data preserved.

tests.description: Acceptance scenarios for create, FX round-trip, and cascade delete.

tests.test_code:
package app

import (
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"gigsynth/internal/db"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// S07-T01: a part edited and saved is recalled identically (sound, mix, split,
// transpose, pan and effects), and recalling it drives the engine.
func TestPartEditorSaveAndRecall(t *testing.T) {
	d, err := db.Open(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "ed.db"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	lib := NewLibrary(d)
	song, _ := d.CreateSong("S")
	part, _ := d.AddPart(song.ID, "P")

	// Edit a scene: layer 0 with a sound, mix, split, transpose and full FX.
	sc := DefaultScene()
	l := &sc.Layers[0]
	l.PresetName, l.Bank, l.Program = "Fender Rhodes", 1, 5
	l.Volume, l.Pan, l.Enabled = 108, 70, true
	l.KeyLow, l.KeyHigh, l.Transpose = 36, 96, 12
	l.ChorusOn, l.ChorusRate, l.ChorusDepth = true, 0.8, 55
	l.DelayOn, l.DelayTime, l.DelayFeedback, l.DelayMix = true, 320, 35, 30

	require.NoError(t, lib.SaveScene(part.ID, "P", sc))

	// Recall and assert every field round-tripped.
	got, err := lib.SceneForPart(part.ID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	g := got.Layers[0]
	assert.Equal(t, "Fender Rhodes", g.PresetName)
	assert.Equal(t, [4]int{1, 5, 108, 70}, [4]int{g.Bank, g.Program, g.Volume, g.Pan})
	assert.Equal(t, [3]int{36, 96, 12}, [3]int{g.KeyLow, g.KeyHigh, g.Transpose})
	assert.True(t, g.ChorusOn)
	assert.Equal(t, 0.8, g.ChorusRate)
	assert.Equal(t, 55, g.ChorusDepth)
	assert.True(t, g.DelayOn)
	assert.Equal(t, [3]int{320, 35, 30}, [3]int{g.DelayTime, g.DelayFeedback, g.DelayMix})

	// Recalling through a controller (with a SoundFont loaded) drives the engine.
	f := &FakeEngine{}
	c := NewController(f, nil)
	require.NoError(t, c.LoadSoundFont("x.sf2"))
	f.Reset()
	c.SetScene(got)
	assert.Contains(t, f.Calls, "SelectProgram ch=0 bank=1 prog=5")
	assert.Contains(t, f.Calls, "CC ch=0 ctrl=7 val=108")
	assert.Contains(t, f.Calls, "CC ch=0 ctrl=10 val=70")
}

package db

import (
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// S07-T02: reordering parts persists their sort_order.
func TestReorderPartsPersists(t *testing.T) {
	d, err := Open(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "ro.db"))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer d.Close()

	s, _ := d.CreateSong("S")
	a, _ := d.AddPart(s.ID, "A")
	b, _ := d.AddPart(s.ID, "B")
	c, _ := d.AddPart(s.ID, "C")

	// Reorder to C, A, B.
	require.NoError(t, d.ReorderParts([]int64{c.ID, a.ID, b.ID}))

	parts, err := d.ListParts(s.ID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Len(t, parts, 3)

	var names []string
	for i, p := range parts {
		names = append(names, p.Name)
		require.Equal(t, i+1, p.SortOrder, "sort_order should be contiguous from 1")
	}
	require.Equal(t, []string{"C", "A", "B"}, names)
}

stories.title: Manufacturer MIDI mappings (CC -> params)
stories.user_story: As a gigging keyboardist, I want per-keyboard manufacturer mapping presets (M-Audio, Behringer, Arturia, Novation, Akai, Generic, Custom) so my controller's sliders/knobs control volume, pan and the chorus/delay knobs in real time.

In Controller.handleMIDI, resolve incoming CC via the bound keyboard's map to actions (set volume/pan/chorus/delay param) instead of blanket-forwarding. Settings exposes preset selection + custom mapping.

stories.fix_solution: New internal/midimap package: per-manufacturer CC->Action maps (Generic GM, M-Audio, Behringer, Arturia, Novation, Akai) with Action enum (Volume/Pan/ChorusRate/ChorusDepth/DelayTime/DelayFeedback/DelayMix/Sustain). Controller now holds a midimap.Map per keyboard slot (default Generic GM) and SetKeyboardMapping(slot,preset) swaps it. handleMIDI ControlChange routes via applyCC: for each keyboard driving a matching layer, mapped CCs call the existing SetLayerVolume/SetLayerPan/SetChorus/SetDelay setters (chorus depth = raw CC value; delay feedback/mix scaled 0..127 -> 0..100; delay time -> 0..1000ms), and unmapped CCs pass through to the engine. stories.title: MP3 backing player (beep)
stories.user_story: As a gigging keyboardist, I want a built-in MP3 player with file select, Start, Stop, Pitch and Loop on the Live view.
stories.description: Add internal/mp3 wrapping github.com/gopxl/beep (mp3 decode + speaker + resampler + loop). Expose a Player with Load/Play/Stop/SetPitch/SetLoop/Position behind an interface so the transport state machine is testable without real audio.
steps_to_reproduce: On Live, Browse to an .mp3
Press Start (plays), Stop (rewinds)
Enable Loop; let it reach the end; it repeats
Set Pitch +2; playback rises ~a tone
acceptance_criteria: beep decodes mp3 and plays via the platform speaker
Stop resets the playhead to 0
Loop restarts at EOF
Pitch maps semitones to a resample ratio (2^(n/12)) without modifying the file
stories.fix_solution: New internal/mp3 package: a transport state machine (Stopped/Playing) with Start/Stop (Stop rewinds playhead to 0), SetLoop (ReachEnd restarts from 0 when looping, else stops), and SetPitch in semitones mapped to a resample ratio of 2^(n/12). Audio is decoupled via an Output interface (Play/Stop/SetRatio/SetLoop) so the real beep backend plugs in while tests run headless with a nil output. Verified by a godog feature (start->playing, stop->stopped+rewind, loop restart, pitch+2 -> ratio ~1.1225) and a unit table test of the semitone->ratio formula (incl. octave = 2.0). Note: the beep audio backend implements Output and is wired in the UI; only the transport/pitch logic is exercised in headless tests.

tests.description: Acceptance scenarios for the player state machine using a fake audio sink.
tests.how_we_test: godog against the Player with a fake/headless sink (no real speaker); assert state transitions, playhead reset, loop wrap, and the pitch->ratio formula.

stories.title: Per-keyboard FX engine architecture
stories.user_story: As a developer, I want an independent effects insert chain per keyboard so each keyboard can have its own chorus and delay (FluidSynth's built-in chorus/reverb are global and it has no delay).
stories.description: Design internal/fx: an Insert chain per keyboard with Chorus and Delay nodes. Decide and implement the audio path: either (a) one FluidSynth instance per keyboard each rendered to a buffer then through the Go DSP inserts and mixed, or (b) post-synth per-channel DSP taps. Define DSP node interfaces and parameter setters used by the Controller.
steps_to_reproduce: Build with the FX package
Route keyboard 1 through chorus+delay and keyboard 2 dry
Confirm keyboard 2 is unaffected by keyboard 1's FX
Toggle a node on/off at runtime
acceptance_criteria: FX inserts are per-keyboard and independent
Chorus and Delay nodes implement a common Node interface (Process + SetParam + Enable)
Enabling/disabling a node is click-free (no zipper noise) and real-time safe
Architecture choice (multi-instance vs DSP tap) is documented in code
stories.fix_solution: New internal/fx package realises per-keyboard effects as Go DSP nodes (each keyboard owns one Chain = Chorus -> Delay), because FluidSynth chorus/reverb are global and it has no delay. Node interface: Process(in-place buffer)/SetEnabled/Enabled/SetParam(human units). Delay = feedback delay line (time ms, feedback pct, mix pct); Chorus = LFO-modulated interpolated delay (rate Hz, depth pct). Both bypass to the dry signal when disabled and allocate nothing in Process. Verified: impulse to decaying echoes at the exact delay time, delay bypass identity, chorus bypass identity, and enabled chorus changes the signal while staying bounded.

tests.name: Delay node produces a delayed tap
tests.description: An impulse into the delay node reappears after Time samples scaled by Mix, with Feedback echoes.
tests.how_we_test: Unit: feed an impulse buffer, assert non-zero sample at the expected delay index and decaying echoes per feedback.

tests.name: Chorus node modulates without changing RMS drastically; bypass is identity
tests.description: When disabled, output equals input sample-for-sample; when enabled, output differs but stays bounded.
tests.how_we_test: Unit: process a sine; assert bypass identity and enabled-output bounded/differs.

stories.title: Per-keyboard Chorus (Rate, Depth)
stories.user_story: As a gigging keyboardist, I want a chorus effect with Rate and Depth knobs plus On/Off on each keyboard, controllable live and stored per part.
stories.description: Wire the fx.Chorus node to each keyboard. Add Controller.SetChorus(kb, on, rate, depth). Persist chorus_on/chorus_rate/chorus_depth per part_channel. Expose two knobs + On in Live/editor and on the small-screen modes.
steps_to_reproduce: On Live, enable Keyboard 1 chorus
Set Rate and Depth; hear the shimmer
Save the part; recall later; chorus returns
Keyboard 2 chorus stays off
acceptance_criteria: Chorus On + Rate + Depth controllable from the UI and via mapped CCs
Per-keyboard independence
State persists in the part and recalls
Defaults: off, rate 0.8 Hz, depth 50%
stories.fix_solution: Added per-keyboard chorus end to end: app.Layer gained chorus fields (on/rate/depth) with defaults; Controller.SetChorus updates the layer and pushes rate/depth/enable to that keyboard's fx.Chain.Chorus; ApplyScene restores chorus to the DSP chain on recall. The new Library maps db.part_channels chorus columns <-> Scene layers, so SaveScene/SceneForPart round-trips it. Godog feature (3 scenarios) covers enable+set params, save-and-recall persistence, and per-keyboard independence (kb1 on leaves kb2 off).

tests.name: Chorus set/persist/independent
tests.description: Acceptance scenarios for enabling, parameterising, persisting and isolating chorus.
tests.how_we_test: godog drives the Controller+Library(in-memory DB); steps set chorus, save/recall the part, and assert per-keyboard independence and round-trip.

    And I set chorus rate to 0.8 and depth to 55

    When I enable chorus on keyboard 1
    Then keyboard 2 chorus remains disabled

stories.title: Per-keyboard Delay (Time, Feedback, Mix)
stories.user_story: As a gigging keyboardist, I want a delay effect with Time, Feedback and Mix knobs plus On/Off on each keyboard, controllable live and stored per part.
stories.description: Wire the fx.Delay node per keyboard. Add Controller.SetDelay(kb, on, time, feedback, mix). Persist delay_on/delay_time/delay_feedback/delay_mix per part_channel. Expose three knobs + On across Live/editor/small-screen modes.
steps_to_reproduce: On Live, enable Keyboard 1 delay
Set Time/Feedback/Mix; hear repeats
Map an encoder to Mix and adjust live
Save+recall the part; delay returns
acceptance_criteria: Delay On + Time + Feedback + Mix controllable from UI and mapped CCs
Per-keyboard independence
State persists in the part and recalls
Defaults: off, 300 ms, feedback 30%, mix 25%
stories.fix_solution: Added per-keyboard delay end to end: app.Layer gained delay fields (on/time/feedback/mix) with defaults; Controller.SetDelay updates the layer and pushes time/feedback/mix/enable to that keyboard's fx.Chain.Delay; ApplyScene restores it on recall; Library round-trips the db delay columns. Live CC control works via S10 mapping (M-Audio Enc2=CC71 -> DelayMix, scaled 0..127 to 0..100). Godog feature (3 scenarios) covers set-three-params, save-and-recall persistence, and a mapped encoder moving delay mix to ~50 from CC value 64.

tests.description: Acceptance scenarios for the three params, persistence, and CC-driven live control.

stories.title: 7-inch touch layout (-mode touch7)
stories.user_story: As a Pi 5 user with a 7\" 800x480 touchscreen, I want a focus-one-keyboard layout so the five chorus/delay knobs stay finger-sized.
stories.description: Add -mode touch7 selecting internal/ui/touch7.go: KB1/KB2/KB3 focus tabs; the focused keyboard shows sound, volume, pan, key tuning and full FX (chorus 2 + delay 3) as large touch knobs; compact part shuttle + transport. Reuses the Controller.
steps_to_reproduce: Run gigsynth -mode touch7 (or auto-detect 800x480)
Tap KB2; its sound and FX come to front
Adjust a large FX knob with a finger
Shuttle parts from the header
acceptance_criteria: Layout fits 800x480 with FX knobs >= ~60px
Focus tabs switch the active keyboard without losing state
All live controls reachable within one tap
Shares Controller logic with the desktop UI
stories.fix_solution: Added the 7-inch focus-one-keyboard layout (internal/ui/touch7.go), selected by `-mode touch7` (wired through main -> ui.Run at 800x480). KB1/KB2/KB3 buttons set the focused keyboard; the view shows that keyboard's sound plus large Chorus (Rate, Depth) and Delay (Time, Feedback, Mix) value labels, refreshed from the controller scene. Verified by a headless Fyne test that focusing KB2 then KB1 shows each keyboard's sound and FX values.

stories.title: Pi Zero LCD kiosk (-mode pizero)
stories.user_story: As a Pi Zero 2 W user, I want a two-row menu + four always-live knobs, single-keyboard operation, an FX page that banks four encoders across chorus/delay, and 61-key part navigation.
stories.description: Add -mode pizero selecting internal/ui/pizero.go (~480x320): Home/Songs/Sounds/FX/Setup screens, four live knobs (vol/pan/pitch/reverb), FX page banking chorus/delay over four encoders, and controller Program/Bank buttons mapped to part/song navigation.
steps_to_reproduce: Run gigsynth -mode pizero
Press the controller's Program+ to go to the next part
Open FX; rotate encoders to change delay; press FX to switch to chorus
Open Sounds; the four knobs still affect the live sound
acceptance_criteria: Two-row menu + four knobs render at ~480x320
61-key Program/Bank buttons navigate parts/songs
FX page banks 5 params over 4 encoders with a Chorus<->Delay toggle
Knobs remain live on every screen
stories.fix_solution: Added the Pi Zero kiosk (internal/ui/pizero.go), selected by `-mode pizero` (main -> ui.Run at 480x320). pizeroVM models the constrained UX: ProgramUp/ProgramDown map the 61-key controller's transport to NextPart/PrevPart; an FX page banks the four encoders between the chorus and delay groups (ToggleFX / FXGroup, Encoder1 drives the highlighted group's first param); VolumeKnob stays live on any screen. buildPiZero renders the two-row menu + status. Verified by a godog feature: Program Up/Down step parts (3->4->3), the delay-group encoder sets delay time and FX toggles to chorus, and the volume knob changes keyboard 1 volume.

tests.description: Acceptance scenarios for keyboard-driven part nav, FX encoder banking, and always-live knobs.
tests.how_we_test: godog drives a pizero view-model over the Controller+Library; steps simulate Program/Bank buttons and encoders, asserting part index, highlighted FX group and live param changes.

stories.title: Routing: key split + transpose + source
stories.user_story: As a gigging keyboardist, I want per-layer key-split range, transpose and source-keyboard routing so I can build splits and stacks across controllers.
stories.description: Harden the existing Controller.routeNote: source match, split range on note-on, transpose with 0..127 clamp, note-off ignores range/mute to avoid stuck notes. Expose split/transpose/source in the part editor.
steps_to_reproduce: Set keyboard 1 layer split C2..B3 and transpose +12
Play C4 -> no sound (out of split); play C2 -> sounds an octave up
Release any held note across a transpose change -> no stuck note
acceptance_criteria: Note-on respects split range and mute; note-off always releases
Transpose clamps to MIDI 0..127 and triggers all-notes-off on change
Source 'All keyboards' or a specific device gates routing
Multiple layers can stack on overlapping ranges
stories.fix_solution: Verified and locked the routing rules in Controller.routeNote: note-on respects key-split range, mute and source-keyboard matching; transpose shifts the played note and drops results outside MIDI 0..127; note-off uses the same transposed key and ignores range/mute so notes always release; and SetLayerTranspose issues AllNotesOff on the channel when transpose changes so nothing sticks across a change. Covered by table tests for split gating, transpose shift/clamp, source gating, clean note-off, and the transpose-flush.

tests.name: Splits, transpose and source gating
tests.description: Note routing honours range/transpose/source and never sticks notes.
tests.how_we_test: Unit/table tests injecting notes across boundaries and a transpose change; assert FakeEngine NoteOn/NoteOff calls.

stories.title: PANIC / all-notes-off safety
stories.user_story: As a gigging keyboardist, I want a PANIC that kills stuck notes and re-applies the mixer so I can always recover on stage.
stories.description: Keep Controller.Panic -> engine system reset + ApplyScene (re-send CC7/CC10). Ensure transpose/mute/enable/recall paths call AllNotesOff appropriately. Bind PANIC to a UI button (all modes) and optionally a controller button.
steps_to_reproduce: Hold notes, trigger a stuck condition
Press PANIC
All sound stops and the mixer levels are restored
acceptance_criteria: PANIC silences all channels immediately
Mixer CCs are re-applied after the reset
Transpose change and part recall do not leave stuck notes
PANIC reachable in Live, touch7 and pizero modes
stories.fix_solution: PANIC path (Controller.Panic) calls the engine reset first then ApplyScene, which re-applies master gain and per-channel CC7 volume / CC10 pan for every layer so the mixer survives the system reset. Test asserts the first engine call is the reset and that the volume/pan CCs for each channel are re-sent afterwards. (Transpose/mute/enable/recall paths already issue AllNotesOff to avoid stuck notes.)

tests.name: PANIC resets then re-applies mixer
tests.description: After Panic, the fake engine shows a system reset followed by CC7/CC10 re-application for active layers.
tests.how_we_test: Unit: enable layers, set volumes, call Panic(); assert the fake call log order (reset, then CCs).
